newsitem.title: USA: Turbulence on Dallas-SLC route hurts 17 - AMR.
newsitem.headline: Turbulence on Dallas-SLC route hurts 17 - AMR.

text.p: Turbulence during two American Airlines flights sent 17 people to hospitals on Thursday.
A spokesman for the airline's parent company, AMR Corp, said 14 passengers and two flight attendants were hurt on a flight from Dallas to Salt Lake City.
Sixty-nine passengers and five crew members were aboard the McDonnell Douglas Super 80, AMR spokesman Tim Smith said.
Turbulence prompted the pilot of the second flight, a Fokker F-100 going from Salt Lake City to Dallas, to land in Amarillo, Texas, Smith said.
He said one person from that flight went to the hospital. It had about 80 people on board.
Smith had no information on the injuries.
Both incidents occurred about midday as the aircraft were flying over the Rocky Mountains. They prompted the airlines to avoid flying through the area for the rest of the day, Smith said.
No other flights were disrupted, Smith said.
The Fokker F-100 is a 97-seat twin-engine aircraft.
Smith said the McDonnell Douglas Super 80 is a 139-seat twin engine and American Airline's most commonly used aircraft.
